items.title: Show HN: OpenArcanum – An End-to-End Encrypted Alternative to Discord
items.summary: A while back I recall being told it can't be done and won't be "Discord". To that, I have to admit, it's not Discord. It isn't designed in a way to profile it's users and it respects privacy. There is still much work to do on this project, but it's in open beta with a web client so people can see how it works before committing to a desktop app download. Mobile apps will come later, if there is proven interest in this platform. I don't care to monitize it. The only thing users will ever see is a non-intrusive "Please donate" badge at most, with the intentions to just keep the maintainer nodes and some official relays running. There are no accounts. There is no way for me to see the messages. It is a platform that respects the user's privacy and asks nothing of it's user's. Anyone can run the entire stack in their own hardware, in private, with no limitations on controlling their data. items.title: Show HN: Sunlight – the camera-based infinite canvas window manager for Mac
items.summary: Hey HN, I'm Darin. You might know me from my work at Webflow (YC S13) and currently Ploy (YC P26). Sunlight is the way I imagined the Mac working before I got my 1st-gen MacBook Air in high school (2008). I had looked at a bunch of Apple videos of Mission Control (Exposé back then) and somehow decided it worked like an infinite canvas. I even told my mom about it! I guess it stuck with me. Windowing on the Mac is so good it's one of those "if it ain't broke don't fix it" things. And yet, it always felt lacking. So Sunlight reimagines it from first principles: - 355"+ virtual desktop - 120fps, fully native - Multi-touch interactions - Guides, grids and haptics - Minimap - ⌘Tab and Mission Control work as usual - Works with your Dock, widgets and desktop - Collision detection and magnetic windows - Tiling and saved layouts - Deeply customizable - ...and much more (including agent support) coming soon Free and open source, forever. Launch demo (2:34): https://youtu.be/NSerIT8zRpw Repo: https://github.com/spacefarm-digital/sunlight

Show HN: Overtone – Transcribe, correct and cut captions for any screen shape
items.summary: Hi HN, I'm Ruud, co-founder of Lont. We turn company emails into personalized videos. Video captions cost us manual work twice: fixing misheard words, then fixing layout, like lines ending on “the”. Overtone uses multiple models to listen to the audio: gpt-transcribe, Azure STT, and Elevenlabs Scribe. When they return conflicting results, Overtone sends small clips to the models again, and then lets an LLM decide what was actually said. The LLM is like a human doing a sanity check on the transcription model. Humans would easily recognize a word to be different based on context. The LLM basically does the same, using an optional context prompt + its world knowledge. Because of this the Word Error Rate (WER) on many test files is lower when using Overtone, compared to just using a model without it. Sure, the cost is higher because we use up to 3 different STT models + an LLM, but it still removes mistakes, reducing the time needed to fix captions to a minimum, and reducing the chance you'll miss something. For us it's worth it. For ultra high volume use cases it may not be. The rules-based cutter nicely cuts the transcript into captions that look good, depending on screen size: 16:9 is different from 9:16, and the Overtone Format we created supports any type really. Pauses become breaks, captions are grouped per speaker, and names/numbers are never spread out over multiple captions. How to add these captions to your videos? A videojs plugin can do this automatically, so you don't burn in your captions. The plugin lets you cycle between styled captions, plain captions, and off. You can burn them into an MP4 file with overtone burn. Quickly try it out just the cutter? Try: npx overtone-captions recut yoursub.srt Transcribing audio with API keys works too. Use --dry-run to show a cost estimate before you send. We open-sourced this first version (MIT) because we believe many people can benefit from this, especially if your captions just need to be good. There's plenty of room to improve though, so we've made it easy to help contribute to add style packs, languages, and providers/models. You can find a demo at: https://overtone.lont.ai/ Find the code and benchmarks here: https://github.com/lonthq/overtone-captions

Show HN: Apgar – Catch agent regressions without an LLM judge
items.summary: Hey HN, We build financial AI agents, and Apgar is the tool we wrote to see whether a harness change made an agent better or worse in production. Our offline evals can't cover every kind of question or session real users bring, and the LLM judge we run in Langfuse is too expensive to use on more than a small slice of traffic, so some failures get through. Apgar is a small release health checker that sits on top of our Langfuse data. It picks up the release from the production traces, and for the first hours of each new release it compares the agent's behavior with the previous release on things like tool calls per turn, retries of the same failing call, loops, output length and cost per turn (11 metrics right now). The release page shows what moved in both directions. When something gets worse, we get a Slack message (and a webhook) saying which metric moved and where the change is concentrated, for example only on Telegram or only in long sessions. We've been running it for a while and decided to open-source it: https://github.com/oimo-ai/apgar It's not meant to be another monitoring tool. We still use Langfuse for that. Apgar only tries to answer "is this release worse than the last one?" It works with Langfuse or with anything that sends OpenTelemetry. There's no LLM judge in it, so it's cheap enough to run on all traffic. The downside is that it can't tell that an answer is wrong if everything else about the turn looks the same. That's still what our evals are for. It runs on Docker Compose (or Helm) with ClickHouse, and it's Apache-2.0. The Agents page can load demo data if you want to try it without connecting anything. Curious how others deal with this. When you change your harness or prompts, how do you find out whether the agent actually got better or worse?
